candidates.next_evidence: Track 2026 capex, N2/A16 capacity ramp, CoWoS capacity CAGR, advanced packaging revenue disclosures, customer prepayments, and commentary on whether supply remains short versus AI demand.
candidates.node_relation: Direct asset owner of leading-edge foundry capacity and advanced packaging platforms including CoWoS, InFO, SoIC, and related 3D/2.5D integration technologies.
candidates.theme_relation: AI accelerators from major fabless customers rely on TSMC leading-edge nodes and advanced packaging; capacity limits at this layer can cap AI GPU/ASIC shipments.
candidates.why_include: TSMC is the clearest public-market mapping for the node because it controls both advanced wafer fabrication and key advanced packaging capacity used in high-performance AI chips.

candidates.next_evidence: Track EUV and High-NA EUV backlog, shipment lead times, China export-control effects, installed-base management revenue, and customer concentration across TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK hynix, and Micron.
candidates.node_relation: Direct supplier of EUV lithography systems required for the most advanced logic and DRAM processes.
candidates.theme_relation: AI infrastructure increases demand for advanced logic, HBM/DRAM, and leading-edge wafer capacity, supporting demand for EUV and related lithography tools.
candidates.why_include: ASML is the obvious lithography choke-point supplier; EUV tool availability, backlog, shipment cadence, and service capacity are key constraints for advanced nodes.

candidates.next_evidence: Track semiconductor systems revenue by market, order commentary tied to leading-edge logic/DRAM/advanced packaging, China exposure, and whether advanced packaging tools grow faster than baseline WFE.
candidates.node_relation: Broad equipment supplier for leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM, materials engineering, and advanced packaging process steps.
candidates.theme_relation: AI compute growth drives advanced-node, HBM, and advanced-packaging equipment intensity, which maps to Applied Materials' semiconductor systems and service businesses.
candidates.why_include: AMAT is a broad, high-scale beneficiary of rising process complexity rather than a single-point bottleneck; include as an enabling equipment leader for the node.

candidates.next_evidence: Track advanced packaging revenue, process-control intensity as a percentage of WFE, foundry/logic and memory customer capex, and management commentary on AI infrastructure demand.
candidates.node_relation: Supplier of process-control and inspection/metrology systems needed to improve yield as leading-edge devices and advanced packaging become more complex.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Semiconductor process control, inspection, and metrology equipment
candidates.theme_relation: AI chips increase die size, packaging complexity, and yield sensitivity; process control can become more valuable as foundries and OSATs ramp advanced nodes and 2.5D/3D packaging.
candidates.why_include: KLAC is not the lithography bottleneck itself, but process control is a second-order choke point when customers push advanced-node and advanced-packaging yields.

candidates.next_evidence: Track customer commitments, Arizona production timeline, capex, utilization, advanced packaging revenue mix, TSMC/Intel/AMD/NVIDIA-related disclosures, and whether capacity is CoWoS-like or lower-complexity packaging.
candidates.node_relation: Direct OSAT provider with advanced packaging and test capabilities; building a large Arizona advanced packaging and test campus.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Outsourced semiconductor assembly, packaging, and test
candidates.theme_relation: If internal foundry advanced-packaging capacity is constrained, OSAT partners with high-volume advanced packaging capability may absorb spillover and support AI-chip supply-chain resilience.
candidates.why_include: Amkor is the most direct US-listed OSAT candidate for advanced-packaging capacity, especially for US supply-chain localization; however, its AI-chip exposure depends on customer ramps, technology qualification, and timing of the Arizona facility.

evidence.claim: TSMC's 2025 annual report says it is developing advanced packaging and 3D chip stacking technologies including CoWoS, InFO, TSMC-SoIC, and COUPE to support customer needs, and notes AI-driven demand for advanced manufacturing capacity.
TSMC's 2025 annual report PDF discusses investing in leading-edge, specialty, and advanced packaging capacity, with AI market developments remaining positive in 2025.
ASML's 2025 annual report states backlog stood at EUR 38.8 billion and that EUV 0.33 NA growth was driven by strong demand in advanced logic and DRAM supporting AI infrastructure buildout.
Applied Materials' 2025 annual report says customer equipment investments are expected to remain strong with growth in high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, AI, and data-center computing demand.

Applied Materials' fiscal 2025 10-K commentary says AI adoption is driving investment in advanced semiconductors and WFE, and that the company is positioned in leading-edge logic, DRAM, and advanced packaging.
KLA's fiscal 2025 stockholder letter says FY25 growth was fueled by AI infrastructure and advanced packaging, with advanced packaging growth in the Semiconductor Process Control segment.
KLA's 2026 results filing says it is a key enabler of the AI ecosystem and benefits across foundry/logic, memory, advanced packaging, and services.

evidence.claim: Amkor said the Arizona project is intended to be the first US-based high-volume advanced packaging facility and to support US AI industry capabilities.

memory_update.text: Core direct candidates for the advanced_foundry_packaging_lithography node: TSM, ASML, AMAT, KLAC, AMKR.
The node appears to split into three investable sub-layers: foundry/packaging asset owners, lithography/WFE tool vendors, and process-control/OSAT capacity enablers.

Next pass should check additional US-listed or ADR candidates not included due to the five-name cap: LRCX, ONTO, ASMIY/ASM International, TOELY/Tokyo Electron, ASX/ASE Technology, UMC, ICHR, COHU, TER, AEHR, FORM, MKSI, ENTG, ACLS, and substrate/interposer suppliers where US listing and market cap are sufficient.

Need separate evidence pass for advanced substrates/interposers because many obvious leaders are Japan/Taiwan-listed rather than primarily US-listed; ADR liquidity and market-cap eligibility should be checked.
Amkor's inclusion is an inference rather than a fully proven AI bottleneck claim because Arizona capacity is not immediate and customer/product mix must be verified through future disclosures.

node: Leading-edge foundry, advanced packaging, and lithography
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI supply-chain node covering leading-edge foundry capacity, advanced packaging, lithography, and enabling wafer-fab/process-control equipment. Highest-direct-exposure candidates are TSMC as the dominant advanced foundry and CoWoS-like packaging asset owner, ASML as the EUV lithography bottleneck supplier, Applied Materials as a broad leading-edge logic/DRAM/advanced-packaging equipment vendor, KLA as process-control/yield equipment exposed to advanced packaging and foundry complexity, and Amkor as a US-listed outsourced advanced packaging and test provider with a large Arizona advanced-packaging buildout. This is research support only and not a buy/sell recommendation.
